Q209530.t: A dun-coloured river with diamonds in its gravels
Q209530.s: Vaal means 'pale' in Afrikaans, and it fits: a dun, silty river winding across flat khaki veld. Around 1870 prospectors found diamonds in its gravels at Klipdrift, today's Barkly West, just before the great Kimberley rush began some 30 km away. Further downstream the Vaal ends in the Orange, as its longest tributary.
Q209530.w: A thin brown line looping across flat, dusty veld north-west of Kimberley, edged by a dark fringe of trees.
f: At about 1,120 km, the Vaal is the longest tributary of the Orange River.
The Vaal Dam, finished in 1938, stores water for Johannesburg and the rest of Gauteng.
Barkly West began as Klipdrift, a camp of diggers washing the river gravels for diamonds.

q.q: Which river does the Vaal flow into?

Q272074.t: Where Oregon Trail wagons finally left the river
Q272074.s: For hundreds of kilometres across Idaho, wagon trains on the Oregon Trail followed this river through dry sagebrush country. Here, at Farewell Bend, they turned away from it for good and struck north-west into the Oregon hills. Downstream the Snake plunges into Hells Canyon, deeper than the Grand Canyon, before it joins the Columbia.
Q272074.w: A blue-green river in a dry, tan valley along the Oregon–Idaho border, widening into a long reservoir to the north.
f: At about 1,735 km, the Snake is the largest tributary of the Columbia River.
Hells Canyon, downstream, is about 2,400 m deep – the deepest river gorge in North America.
Shoshone Falls on the Snake in southern Idaho drop about 65 m, more than Niagara.

q.q: Which river does the Snake flow into?

Q142148.t: Brazil's 'Old Chico', crossing the dry backlands
Q142148.s: Brazilians call it Velho Chico, Old Chico, and it earns the affection: it carries water right across the dry sertão, where many rivers run only in the rainy season. Here in northern Minas Gerais it winds north through scrub and cattle country, flanked by pale sandbars. Its name dates from 4 October 1501, St Francis's day, when Portuguese ships reached its mouth.
Q142148.w: A wide, sandy-banked river winding north through olive-brown scrub, with long pale sandbars in the dry season.
f: At roughly 2,800 km, it is the longest river that flows entirely within Brazil.
Its Sobradinho reservoir in Bahia covers over 4,000 km², one of the largest artificial lakes on Earth.
Boatmen once fixed carved wooden heads called carrancas to their bows to ward off river spirits.

q.q: What do Brazilians fondly call the São Francisco?

Q82812.t: A northern river that sometimes flows backwards
Q82812.s: In spring the Sukhona can do something strange: when its tributary the Vologda is in full flood, its upper course runs backwards into Lake Kubenskoye. Here it winds past Totma through dark taiga and hay meadows. Totma sent many men to sea, among them Ivan Kuskov, who in 1812 founded Fort Ross in California.
Q82812.w: A narrow dark river looping through unbroken taiga, with pale strips of meadow along its banks and small Totma on a bend.
f: At Veliky Ustyug the Sukhona meets the Yug, and together they form the Northern Dvina.
Below Totma the river cuts through the Opoki, high cliffs of pale rock where rapids once scared boatmen.
About 560 km long, the Sukhona carried the old trade route from Vologda to Arkhangelsk.

q.q: Which California outpost did Totma-born Ivan Kuskov found?

Q15277375.t: One of the Yenisei's first threads, in a lost valley
Q15277375.s: Few rivers start as remotely as this. The Shishged gathers its water in the Darkhad basin, a flat valley about 1,600 m up, ringed by larch-covered ranges and scattered with lakes. From here it slips north into Siberia and becomes one of the headwaters of the Yenisei, which reaches the Arctic Ocean thousands of kilometres away.
Q15277375.w: A wide flat valley speckled with small lakes, ringed by dark forested mountains, one range west of long blue Lake Khövsgöl.
f: Ice-age glaciers dammed the Darkhad basin more than once, filling it with a large lake.
Dukha reindeer herders, also called Tsaatan, live in the taiga around the valley.
Across the border in Tuva it continues as the Kyzyl-Khem, then as the Little Yenisei.

q.q: Which great river does the Shishged help to start?

Q776155.t: One of the two rivers that make the Paraná
Q776155.s: Pastures, coffee and soya fields spread across these uplands, and through them the Paranaíba runs in a green, wooded groove. Downstream it is barely a river any more but a chain of big reservoirs, one after another, along the border of Goiás and Minas Gerais. Where it finally meets the Rio Grande, the two become the Paraná.
Q776155.w: A thin, tree-lined river in a patchwork of green and red-brown fields; further west it swells into long branching reservoirs.
f: The Paranaíba is roughly 1,000 km long and marks much of the border between Goiás and Minas Gerais.
Dams such as Emborcação, Itumbiara and São Simão turn its lower course into a staircase of lakes.
It is easy to confuse with the Parnaíba, a different river that reaches the Atlantic in north-east Brazil.

q.q: The Paranaíba joins which river to form the Paraná?

Q31379.t: A wild taiga river rebuilt as a chain of giant lakes
Q31379.s: What looks like a string of vast, ragged lakes across the taiga is a river remade by engineers. Since the 1970s the La Grande has been dammed step by step for hydropower, and neighbouring rivers were diverted into it, roughly doubling its flow. In winter the reservoirs freeze into white shapes with drowned, fingered shorelines.
Q31379.w: Huge irregular reservoirs full of islands and inlets in dark spruce forest, strung east to west towards James Bay.
f: The turbines of the Robert-Bourassa power station sit in a cavern about 140 m underground.
Its spillway is cut into ten giant steps and is nicknamed the Giant's Staircase.
The river is about 900 km long and empties into James Bay.

q.q: What is the stepped spillway on the La Grande nicknamed?

Q80240.t: A steppe river long drawn as Europe's edge
Q80240.s: Loops, oxbows and crescent lakes crowd the Ural's floodplain here, a ribbon of dark woodland across bare, sunburnt steppe. The river runs about 2,400 km from the Ural Mountains to the Caspian, and many maps use it as part of the line between Europe and Asia. Until 1775 it was called the Yaik.
Q80240.w: A tightly meandering river with bright oxbow lakes and a dark strip of floodplain forest across flat yellow-brown steppe.
f: Catherine the Great renamed the Yaik in 1775, after Pugachev's rebellion broke out among its Cossacks.
Pushkin came to Uralsk in 1833 to collect memories of Pugachev for his book on the revolt.
Its lower course has no dams, so Caspian sturgeon can still swim upstream to spawn.

q.q: What was the Ural River called before 1775?

Q3047.t: The 'swift-flowing river' of the fur-trade canoes
Q3047.s: The name comes from a Cree phrase for 'swift-flowing river', and for generations it was a highway for fur-trade canoes heading west. Here, near The Pas, the current slows and spreads into a vast delta of channels, marshes and lakes. Downstream the river ends in Lake Winnipeg, carrying water that fell as snow on the Rockies.
Q3047.w: A brown river snaking through a maze of marsh, reed beds and shallow lakes on a flat, forested plain.
f: The Saskatchewan River Delta, around 10,000 km², is one of the largest inland deltas in North America.
Cumberland House, the Hudson's Bay Company's first inland post, was built on this river in 1774.
The river is born where the North and South Saskatchewan meet, east of Prince Albert.

q.q: What does the Cree name behind 'Saskatchewan' mean?

Q217818.t: A Rhine branch strung with old Hanseatic towns
Q217818.s: Of the Rhine's three Dutch branches, the IJssel is the one that turns north. It winds for about 125 km through green floodplain between dikes, past brick towns that grew rich in the Hanseatic League: Doesburg, Zutphen, Deventer, Kampen. It ends close to the lake that bears its name, the IJsselmeer, once the salty Zuiderzee.
Q217818.w: A winding river in a wide green floodplain between dikes, with the compact town of Deventer on its east bank.
f: IJ counts as a single letter in Dutch, so both letters are capitalised: IJssel, IJsselmeer.
Deventer, Zutphen and Kampen on the IJssel were all members of the Hanseatic League.
Under the Room for the River programme, side channels were dug here so floods can spread safely.

q.q: Why is IJssel written with two capital letters?
q.a: IJ is one letter in Dutch

Q40855.t: Europe's fourth-longest river, still young here
Q40855.s: Here the Dnieper is still a modest river, meandering through flat fields and pine woods, with silver oxbows marking its old beds. It has a long way to go: about 2,200 km in all, through three countries to the Black Sea. A thousand years ago this was part of the trade route 'from the Varangians to the Greeks'.
Q40855.w: A modest winding river with silvery oxbow lakes, crossing a flat patchwork of fields and dark pine forest.
f: Among Europe's rivers only the Volga, the Danube and the Ural are longer.
It rises in the Valdai Hills, not far from the sources of the Volga and the Western Dvina.
Gogol wrote that rare is the bird that can fly to the middle of the Dnieper.

q.q: Which sea does the Dnieper flow into?

Q2237.t: Glacier water crossing the prairie city of Edmonton
Q2237.s: The water here set out as meltwater from the Saskatchewan Glacier on the Columbia Icefield, high in the Rockies. By Edmonton it has become a broad, silty river in a deep, wooded valley that snakes right through the city, lined with parks and trails. From here it keeps heading east for hundreds of kilometres across the prairie.
Q2237.w: A brown river in a deep, tree-filled valley winding through Edmonton's grid of streets, then out across flat farmland.
f: The river runs roughly 1,300 km from the Rockies to its meeting with the South Saskatchewan.
The first Fort Edmonton, a fur-trade post, was built on its banks in 1795.
Its valley in Edmonton is one of the longest continuous stretches of urban parkland in North America.

q.q: Where does the North Saskatchewan begin?
x: A spring in the Cypress Hills

Q180558.t: The 'black river' that becomes the Senegal
Q180558.s: Bafing means 'black river', and its partner, the Bakoye, is the 'white river'. They meet at Bafoulabé, whose name means 'meeting of two rivers', and from there on the stream is called the Senegal. Upstream, the Bafing drains the rainy Fouta Djallon highlands; the Manantali dam holds it back in a wide, branching lake.
Q180558.w: A dark ribbon through wooded savanna and red laterite hills; to the north, the long branching Manantali reservoir.
f: The Bafing rises in Guinea's Fouta Djallon, the highlands that also feed the Niger and the Gambia.
The Manantali dam, completed in the late 1980s, created one of the largest reservoirs in West Africa.
Counted from the Bafing's source, the Senegal is about 1,600 km long.

q.q: What does the name Bafing mean?

Q8168.t: An undammed northern giant running to the Barents Sea
Q8168.s: No dam stands anywhere on the Pechora's main stream, and from the air it shows: a broad, braided river of sandbars and wooded islands, running free through taiga toward the Barents Sea. It rises in the northern Urals and flows about 1,800 km. For roughly half the year it is frozen into a white road through the forest.
Q8168.w: A wide river split by sandbanks and wooded islands, winding north through dark taiga and pale bogs, the Urals to the east.
f: The Virgin Komi Forests in its upper basin became Russia's first natural World Heritage site in 1995.
Atlantic salmon still run up the Pechora to spawn.
It ends in a wide delta near Naryan-Mar, opening into the shallow Pechora Sea.

q.q: Which sea does the Pechora flow into?

Q10362010.t: A palm-named stream feeding an inland sea
Q10362010.s: Red earth, cattle pasture and patches of cerrado scrub make up this upland of Minas Gerais, and the Indaiá threads through it in a dark line of gallery forest. It takes its name from a native palm. Its water flows into Três Marias, a huge reservoir on the São Francisco, joining it from the west bank.
Q10362010.w: A narrow dark line of riverside forest across red and green uplands, flowing north into the branching arms of Três Marias.
f: Indaiá is the Brazilian name of a native palm; the town of Dores do Indaiá, in its basin, shares it.
The Três Marias reservoir it feeds holds around 21 billion cubic metres of water.
The cerrado it crosses is considered the most species-rich savanna on Earth.

q.q: Which reservoir does the Indaiá flow into?

Q3334104.t: A wild gorge river racing to become the Irrawaddy
Q3334104.s: This river has two names and hardly a calm stretch. In China it is the Dulong, home of the Derung people; in Myanmar it becomes the N'Mai Hka, a fast, cold torrent hidden deep among steep forested ridges. North of Myitkyina it merges with the Mali Hka, and together they form the Irrawaddy.
Q3334104.w: A thin silvery line deep in a maze of steep green ridges running north to south, often patched with cloud.
f: The meeting point with the Mali Hka is called Myitsone, Burmese for 'confluence'.
The Derung of its upper valley number only a few thousand, one of China's smallest ethnic groups.
Ridges above its valley rise to more than 3,000 m.

q.q: The N'Mai Hka joins which river to form the Irrawaddy?

Q191829.t: Colombia's river road between two Andean ranges
Q191829.s: Two ranges of the Andes wall in this valley, and down its middle runs Colombia's great river, broad and brown, heading north for the Caribbean. For centuries the Magdalena was the country's main road: goods and travellers went by boat between the coast and the highlands. García Márquez sent Simón Bolívar on his last journey down it in The General in His Labyrinth.
Q191829.w: A wide brown river with pale sandbars running north down a hot, flat valley between two mountain walls.
f: About 1,500 km long, the Magdalena reaches the Caribbean at Barranquilla.
Most Colombians live within its basin.
Rapids at Honda, a little downstream, once forced boats to unload and cargo to go round overland.

q.q: Which novelist sent Bolívar down the Magdalena in a novel?

Q1472009.t: A thin green line through the mesas of Patagonia
Q1472009.s: Brown, flat-topped mesas and grey steppe stretch in every direction, and the Neuquén cuts through them in a thin green line. It is fed by snow on the Andes near Domuyo, the highest peak in Patagonia. Downstream its water fills the big artificial lakes of Cerros Colorados, then meets the Limay to form the Río Negro.
Q1472009.w: A narrow river with a green fringe winding south-east through bare, brown plateau; further on, large blue reservoirs in the desert.
f: Domuyo, near its headwaters, rises to about 4,700 m and is often called the roof of Patagonia.
Water from the Neuquén fills Los Barreales and Mari Menuco, two large lakes of the Cerros Colorados scheme.
Neuquén province is rich in dinosaur fossils, including some of the largest ever found.

q.q: Which city stands where the Neuquén meets the Limay?

Q1569231.t: The top of the Pearl River, winding through karst
Q1569231.s: Karst country: green valleys studded with steep limestone hills, red soil and terraced fields, and the Nanpan winding between them. This is the uppermost reach of the Pearl River system. The river rises on Maxiong Mountain in eastern Yunnan, flows south, then swings east in a wide arc before meeting the Beipan to become the Hongshui.
Q1569231.w: A winding river among red-soiled fields and lumpy green limestone hills, in a broad upland of eastern Yunnan.
f: A spring on Maxiong Mountain near Qujing is officially marked as the source of the Pearl River.
The Nanpan is roughly 900 km long.
Its partner the Beipan – the North Pan – joins it on the Guizhou–Guangxi border.

q.q: Which river system does the Nanpan belong to?

Q1471.t: The river that draws Paris in one long arc
Q1471.s: Paris is easy to read even from cruise height: a vast grey-beige city with the Seine drawing one long, gentle arc through its middle. On a clear day you may pick out the split in the stream at its heart, the Île de la Cité, where the city began. Beyond the suburbs the river loops back and forth in huge meanders on its way to the sea.
Q1471.w: A dark river curving east to west through a vast grey city, then looping in big meanders to the north-west.
f: The banks of the Seine in central Paris have been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1991.
Paris's coat of arms shows a ship, a nod to the medieval guild of river merchants who ran the city.
The Seine is about 775 km long and rises on the Langres plateau in Burgundy.

q.q: Which island in the Seine is the historic heart of Paris?

Q552.t: A wandering river fringed with floodplain forest
Q552.s: Silver loops, oxbow lakes and dark bands of riverside forest mark the Oder as it swings north-west across the Silesian lowland. It rises in the hills of Czechia and runs about 840 km to the Baltic, forming part of the border between Germany and Poland on the way. Upstream, Wrocław is built across its islands and branches.
Q552.w: A broad meandering river with bright oxbow lakes and strips of dark floodplain woods, across flat fields and villages.
f: Wrocław, on the Oder, has more than 100 bridges and footbridges.
The river reaches the sea through the Szczecin Lagoon, a large shallow bay behind the Baltic coast.
Its source lies in the Oder Mountains of Czechia, at about 630 m.

q.q: Which sea does the Oder flow into?

Q3569.t: A green ribbon between Senegal and Mauritania
Q3569.s: Rice paddies and gardens make a green stripe along the Senegal River, and beyond it the land turns dry and tawny in both directions. For hundreds of kilometres the river forms the border between Senegal and Mauritania. Its floods once spread across the whole valley floor each rainy season, and farmers still plant the damp land as the water drops back.
Q3569.w: A winding river with bright green, rectangular fields along both banks, set in dry, sandy-brown country.
f: Near its mouth the river runs behind the Langue de Barbarie, a long, thin sand spit, before reaching the Atlantic.
The old colonial town of Saint-Louis, on an island near the mouth, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
The Diama dam near the mouth, finished in the 1980s, stops salty seawater from pushing upstream.

q.q: Which country faces Senegal across the Senegal River?

Q1511505.t: Half of the Yenisei, hurrying to meet the other half
Q1511505.s: Tuvans call it the Ka-Khem. It comes down from Mongolia and runs west through wooded mountains in a chain of rapids and gravel islands. At Kyzyl it meets the Great Yenisei, and from that confluence on the river is simply the Yenisei, one of the longest on Earth, heading north for the Arctic Ocean.
Q1511505.w: A river of gravel bars and braided channels in a mountain valley, dark taiga on the slopes, flowing west towards the Tuvan basin.
f: An obelisk marking the 'Centre of Asia' stands at the confluence in Kyzyl.
The Little Yenisei is about 560 km long.
Its headwaters lie in Mongolia's Darkhad basin, west of Lake Khövsgöl.

q.q: In which city do the Great and Little Yenisei meet?

Q35591.t: A palm-green thread through the Mesopotamian plain
Q35591.s: A narrow band of palm groves and fields follows the Tigris, and on either side the plain fades to sand and stone. This is Mesopotamia, the 'land between the rivers', where some of the first cities rose. Tikrit stands on the bank here; Saladin, who became sultan of Egypt and Syria, was born in the town around 1137.
Q35591.w: A dark ribbon of river with a thin green fringe of palms and fields, winding south through pale desert.
f: The Tigris runs about 1,850 km from the mountains of south-eastern Turkey to its meeting with the Euphrates.
Upstream stood Assur and Nineveh, capitals of ancient Assyria, both on its banks.
Baghdad grew up on the Tigris, founded in 762 as a round city.

q.q: Which famous sultan was born in Tikrit on the Tigris?

Q8187.t: Sandbanks and taiga on the road to the White Sea
Q8187.s: Pale sandbanks and long green islands split the Northern Dvina into several channels as it winds north through the taiga. Born at Veliky Ustyug from the Sukhona and the Yug, it runs about 740 km to the White Sea at Arkhangelsk. Before St Petersburg was built, this river was Russia's main route to sea trade with Western Europe.
Q8187.w: A wide, pale-brown river with sandbanks and wooded islands, winding north through dark taiga and scattered villages.
f: Mikhail Lomonosov was born in 1711 in a village near Kholmogory, on the Dvina's lower course.
Arkhangelsk, near the mouth, was founded in 1584 and became Russia's first major seaport.
The Vaga, one of its largest tributaries, flows in a little upstream of here.

q.q: Which scientist was born near Kholmogory on the Northern Dvina?

Q204806.t: The Niger's great partner, wide and sandy
Q204806.s: In the dry season the Benue looks like a braid of thin channels across a broad bed of pale sand; after the rains it fills from bank to bank and spills onto its floodplain. It rises in Cameroon and runs about 1,400 km before meeting the Niger at Lokoja, where the two rivers join in a giant Y.
Q204806.w: A wide, pale sandy riverbed with braided channels and a green floodplain, winding west across flat savanna.
f: The Benue is the largest tributary of the Niger.
In the flood season, steamers once travelled up it as far as Garoua in Cameroon.
Lagdo dam in northern Cameroon holds back its upper course in a large reservoir.

q.q: Which river does the Benue join at Lokoja?

Q817337.t: A green irrigated valley slicing through grey steppe
Q817337.s: The contrast is stark: a strip of poplars, orchards and fields a few kilometres wide, and beyond it grey-brown Patagonian steppe as far as the eye can see. The Río Negro begins where the Neuquén and the Limay meet, then runs about 635 km across Patagonia to the Atlantic. Its valleys grow most of Argentina's apples and pears.
Q817337.w: A winding blue-green river inside a narrow green valley of fields and tree rows, cut into a flat grey-brown plateau.
f: It carries more water than any other river in Patagonia.
Tall rows of poplars shelter the orchards from the strong Patagonian wind.
Near its mouth, the towns of Viedma and Carmen de Patagones face each other across the river.

q.q: Which fruits is the Río Negro valley best known for?

Q1152951.t: A quiet Rhine branch between forest and orchards
Q1152951.s: North of the river rise the wooded, sandy hills of the Veluwe; south of it lies the Betuwe, flat and neatly lined with orchards. Between them runs the Nederrijn, the 'Lower Rhine', one of the branches into which the great river splits after entering the Netherlands. Weirs manage its flow, deciding how much Rhine water goes on to the IJssel.
Q1152951.w: A modest river with green floodplains between dikes, dark forest to the north and a neat grid of orchards to the south.
f: Past Wijk bij Duurstede the same river takes another name, the Lek.
The weir at Driel controls how much Rhine water flows on towards the IJssel.
The Veluwe to the north is one of the largest forested areas in the Netherlands.

q.q: What is the Nederrijn called below Wijk bij Duurstede?

Q1143852.t: A Rhine branch ending by the windmills of Kinderdijk
Q1143852.s: Pastures below sea level, long straight ditches and dikes: this is the heart of polder country, and the Lek runs through it on its last kilometres. At Kinderdijk it meets the Noord, and the two carry on towards Rotterdam as the Nieuwe Maas. Nineteen 18th-century windmills there once pumped the surrounding polders dry.
Q1143852.w: A broad river between dikes, with flat green polders cut by straight silver ditches on both sides and Rotterdam's sprawl to the west.
f: The Kinderdijk windmills became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1997.
The Lek is about 60 km long, from Wijk bij Duurstede to Kinderdijk.
Much of the land along its lower course lies below sea level.

q.q: Which river does the Lek meet at Kinderdijk?

Q2076850.t: Tigris water carried south to Sumer's plain
Q2076850.s: Also known as the Shatt al-Gharraf, this waterway leaves the Tigris at Kut and runs south across the flat, dusty plain of southern Iraq. Irrigation channels branch off it like the veins of a leaf, feeding date groves and fields. The ruins of the Sumerian cities of Girsu and Lagash lie in the plain near its lower course.
Q2076850.w: A thin dark waterway running south across a pale flat plain, with a green lace of irrigated fields along it.
f: A barrage across the Tigris at Kut sends water into it.
Near its end it splits into smaller channels that fade into the southern marshes.
Excavations at Girsu began in 1877 and revealed one of the oldest cities in the world.

q.q: Which river does the Shatt al-Hayy branch off?

Q615328.t: The 'red water river' of Guangxi's karst
Q615328.s: Hongshui means 'red water', and in the rainy season its current runs rusty with silt from the red soils upstream. Here it snakes through deep karst country, between rows of steep, forested limestone peaks. Formed by the Nanpan and the Beipan, it is stepped with big hydropower dams, among them Longtan, one of the largest in China.
Q615328.w: A winding river in a deep valley, lumpy green limestone peaks crowding both banks and long reservoirs behind dams.
f: The Hongshui forms the main upper course of the Xi River, the chief branch of the Pearl.
Downstream it meets the Liu River and continues as the Qian.
Its cascade of dams, including Yantan and Longtan, makes it one of China's great hydropower rivers.

q.q: What does the name Hongshui mean?

Q2509519.t: A short link in the Pearl River's chain, with a gorge
Q2509519.s: This short river begins where two big Guangxi streams, the Hongshui and the Liu, have just combined. It pushes south-east through low green hills and sugarcane fields, then squeezes through Datengxia, the Great Rattan Gorge, before meeting the Yu River at Guiping. There the name changes again, to the Xun.
Q2509519.w: A wide brown river winding between low green hills and fields, entering a narrow gorge above the town of Guiping.
f: A large dam now closes the Datengxia gorge for flood control, power and shipping.
Guangxi grows more sugarcane than any other province of China.
The Taiping Rebellion broke out in 1851 at Jintian, in the hills near Guiping.

q.q: Which two rivers join to form the Qian?

Q856509.t: The last stretch before the Xi River begins
Q856509.s: Cargo barges ply this broad brown river, one of the busiest waterways of southern China. The Xun begins at Guiping, where the Qian and the Yu meet, and flows east through rolling green hills and fish ponds. At Wuzhou it takes in the Gui River from Guilin, and from there on it is called the Xi, the main stem of the Pearl River.
Q856509.w: A broad brown river bending east through low green hills, with fish ponds and small towns along its banks.
f: The Gui River that joins it at Wuzhou flows down from the karst landscapes of Guilin.
Wuzhou has long been Guangxi's gateway for river trade with Guangzhou and Hong Kong.
Fish ponds line its floodplain, a checkerboard of silver rectangles when the sun catches them.

q.q: At which city does the Xun become the Xi River?

Q584.t: Where the Rhine leaves the hills for the open plain
Q584.s: Here the Rhine is leaving the hills behind. The dark wooded knobs of the Siebengebirge, old volcanoes, crowd its east bank, while to the north the valley opens into the flat, busy lowland towards Cologne. Bonn stands on the west bank: Beethoven was born there in 1770, and from 1949 to 1990 it was West Germany's capital.
Q584.w: A broad, busy river heading north-west, with wooded volcanic hills on its east bank and the city of Bonn along the west.
f: The Rhine is about 1,230 km long, from the Swiss Alps to the North Sea.
Upstream between Bingen and Koblenz, its castle-lined gorge is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
A rack railway has climbed the Drachenfels in the Siebengebirge since 1883.

q.q: Which composer was born in Bonn on the Rhine?

Q216171.t: The Rhine's main branch, running out to the sea
Q216171.s: Most of the Rhine's water takes this route: about two-thirds of it flows into the Waal soon after the river enters the Netherlands. The Waal runs west past Nijmegen, one of the oldest Dutch towns, carrying some of Europe's heaviest barge traffic. Its water finally reaches the North Sea through wide estuaries such as the Haringvliet, closed off by a long dam with sluices.
Q216171.w: A broad grey-blue estuary between flat green islands, shut off from the North Sea to the west by a long dam.
f: Nijmegen on the Waal grew from a Roman settlement and celebrated its 2,000th anniversary in 2005.
The Haringvliet dam, finished in 1971, has huge sluices that let river water out to sea.
The Waal is one of the busiest inland waterways in the world.

q.q: What share of the Rhine's water flows into the Waal?

Q639478.t: The small arm wrapped around a giant river island
Q639478.s: The Javaés is the Araguaia's 'smaller arm': it splits off from the main river and loops round the east side of Bananal Island before rejoining it. That island, around 20,000 km² of flooded grassland and forest, is usually called the largest river island in the world. In the rainy season much of it disappears under water.
Q639478.w: A winding dark river along the east edge of a vast flat island of green savanna and lakes, the wider Araguaia to the west.
f: Brazilians also call it the Braço Menor, the 'smaller arm' of the Araguaia.
The river is named after the Javaé people, who live on Bananal Island.
Araguaia National Park covers the northern part of the island.

q.q: What is Bananal Island, wrapped by the Javaés, usually called?

Q10965.t: The river that gave Iberia its name
Q10965.s: Iberia takes its name from this river, which the Romans knew as the Iberus. Near Tudela it runs through a green belt of orchards and vegetable fields, while just to the north lies the Bardenas Reales, a startling badland desert of pale, eroded clay. The Ebro flows about 910 km from Cantabria to its delta on the Mediterranean.
Q10965.w: A green river valley of fields and orchards, with the pale, furrowed desert of the Bardenas Reales spreading just to the north.
f: It is the longest river flowing entirely within Spain.
Its delta on the Mediterranean is carpeted with rice fields.
Zaragoza, downstream, grew from a Roman colony named after the emperor Caesar Augustus.

q.q: Which peninsula is named after the Ebro?

Q1139679.t: A great jungle river through the old Maya world
Q1139679.s: Broad, green-brown and full of loops, the Usumacinta slides out of the hills onto the flat, wet plain of Tabasco here. Upstream it forms the border between Mexico and Guatemala, and Maya cities stood on its banks: Yaxchilán sits inside a tight loop of the river. Together with the Grijalva, it carries more water than any other river system in Mexico.
Q1139679.w: A wide, muddy river swinging in big loops across a flat green plain of pasture, lagoons and patches of forest.
f: The easiest way to reach Yaxchilán is still by boat along the river.
It rises in the highlands of Guatemala and runs about 1,000 km to the Gulf of Mexico.
Near the coast it joins the Grijalva in a vast maze of wetlands, the Pantanos de Centla.

q.q: Which Maya city lies inside a loop of the Usumacinta?

Q1644.t: Meadows, oxbows and brick towns on a wild-edged river
Q1644.s: Wide meadows, oxbow ponds and patches of floodplain forest line the Elbe here, and for long stretches no town crowds its banks. Tangermünde, a red-brick Hanseatic town, sits on a low bluff above the water. The river rises in the Czech mountains and runs about 1,100 km to the North Sea, passing Dresden, Magdeburg and Hamburg.
Q1644.w: A broad river winding north-west through wide green meadows, with silver oxbow ponds and a small town on its west bank.
f: Near Magdeburg a canal crosses the Elbe on a 918 m water bridge, one of the longest in the world.
Much of its middle course is protected as the UNESCO biosphere reserve River Landscape Elbe.
The Elbe rises in the Krkonoše, or Giant Mountains, at about 1,400 m.

q.q: What crosses the Elbe near Magdeburg on a bridge?

Q2416760.t: A green oasis of trees far out in the tundra
Q2416760.s: Out here the tundra runs to the horizon, a lake-freckled plain of greens and browns, white for most of the year. Yet the Thelon valley holds pockets of spruce far north of the treeline, an oasis that shelters muskoxen, moose and caribou. The river flows east into a string of big lakes and on to Hudson Bay via Chesterfield Inlet.
Q2416760.w: A river threading a chain of long lakes across treeless, lake-speckled tundra, with dark patches of spruce along parts of the valley.
f: The Thelon Wildlife Sanctuary was created in 1927 to protect the region's muskoxen.
The Thelon was named a Canadian Heritage River in 1990.
Its water reaches Hudson Bay through Baker Lake and Chesterfield Inlet.

q.q: Which animal was the Thelon sanctuary created to protect?

ne-rv-1159112855.t: The Colorado when it was still called the Grand
ne-rv-1159112855.s: Until 1921 this stretch was called the Grand River, and the city of Grand Junction is named after its meeting with the Gunnison. From above, the Colorado is a green irrigated strip of orchards and vineyards between the grey terraces of the Book Cliffs and the high, flat top of Grand Mesa. Canyon country begins just downstream.
ne-rv-1159112855.w: A green strip of fields and a small city along the river, grey cliffs to the north, a huge flat mesa to the east.
f: Grand Mesa, to the east, is often called the largest flat-topped mountain in the world.
The Colorado runs about 2,330 km from the Rockies towards the Gulf of California.
Palisade, just upstream, is known for its peaches and wine.

q.q: What was this stretch of the Colorado called until 1921?

Q386331.t: A staircase of reservoirs between two Brazilian states
Q386331.s: The Rio Grande here is less a river than a staircase of lakes: dam after dam holds it back in long, branching reservoirs between São Paulo and Minas Gerais. Around them stretch sugarcane, soy and pasture, laid out in huge geometric fields. Further west it joins the Paranaíba, and from that meeting on the river is called the Paraná.
Q386331.w: A wide, branching reservoir along a state border, ringed by vast rectangular fields of green cane and red earth.
f: It rises in the Serra da Mantiqueira and runs about 1,300 km.
The Furnas dam upstream, finished in the 1960s, was one of Brazil's first big hydropower projects.
For much of its course it forms the border between the states of São Paulo and Minas Gerais.

q.q: What do people in Minas Gerais call the vast Furnas reservoir?

Q14294.t: The river that wraps itself around Toledo
Q14294.s: Toledo is built on a rocky hill that the Tagus almost surrounds, curling round it in a deep, tight gorge. From cruise height the loop shows as a sharp bend in a green river crossing the tawny Castilian plain. The Tagus is the longest river of the Iberian Peninsula, flowing about 1,000 km to the Atlantic at Lisbon.
Q14294.w: A green river making a sharp horseshoe bend around a compact hilltop city in brown, dry plain.
f: The old city of Toledo has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1986.
Its estuary at Lisbon is so wide that part of it is called the Sea of Straw.
Upstream, the royal palace town of Aranjuez was built in a green bend of the river.

q.q: At which city does the Tagus reach the Atlantic?

Q548.t: Poland's great river, still braided with sandbanks
Q548.s: Sandbars, willow islands and shallow side channels give the Vistula a wild look, even this close to Warsaw. It is Poland's longest river, running about 1,050 km from the Silesian Beskids past Kraków and Warsaw to the Baltic near Gdańsk. Much of its course is still unregulated, which is rare for a river this size in Europe.
Q548.w: A wide river with pale sandbars and green willow islands, running north through a flat patchwork of fields towards Warsaw.
f: The Vistula basin covers more than half of Poland.
Kraków's Wawel Castle stands on a hill above the Vistula.
Near the sea its branches built the flat Żuławy delta, parts of which lie below sea level.

q.q: Near which city does the Vistula reach the Baltic?

Q193737.t: A river bending into a moccasin at Chattanooga
Q193737.s: Look for a huge meander shaped like a foot: Moccasin Bend, where the Tennessee coils round a flat peninsula beneath Lookout Mountain. Chattanooga spreads along its banks between wooded ridges. The river runs a strange U-shaped course, south into Alabama, then west and north across Tennessee and Kentucky to the Ohio.
Q193737.w: A tight, foot-shaped loop of river beside a city, with a long wooded ridge rising just to the south-west.
f: Since 1933 the Tennessee Valley Authority has turned the river into a chain of dammed lakes.
The Tennessee is about 1,050 km long and joins the Ohio at Paducah, Kentucky.
Muscle Shoals, downstream in Alabama, gave its name to a famous recording scene.

q.q: Which river does the Tennessee join at Paducah?

Q483159.t: The ancient Jaxartes, winding through rice and desert
Q483159.s: A green, glinting strip of rice paddies and reed marsh follows the Syr Darya across the desert, with the Kyzylkum sands spreading to the south. The river, known to the Greeks as the Jaxartes, runs about 2,200 km from the Tian Shan to the North Aral Sea. A dike built there in 2005 has helped that part of the shrunken sea to refill.
Q483159.w: A meandering river in a green belt of flooded rice fields and reeds, with pale desert sand to the south.
f: Further downstream, the Baikonur Cosmodrome stands near its banks.
It is formed in the Fergana Valley, where the Naryn and the Kara Darya meet.
Alexander the Great founded Alexandria Eschate, 'the Furthest', on its banks in 329 BC.

q.q: What did the ancient Greeks call the Syr Darya?

Q651195.t: A glacier-fed torrent in the heart of the Tian Shan
Q651195.s: Snow-capped ranges, bare brown slopes and a thin grey-green river at the bottom of the valley: this is the Naryn in the heart of the Tian Shan. The town of Naryn stretches along the river for kilometres. Fed by glaciers, the river runs west into the long Toktogul reservoir, then out to the Fergana Valley, where it becomes the Syr Darya.
Q651195.w: A thin river in a narrow valley between bare brown ranges, snow on the peaks and a long strip of town along its banks.
f: The Toktogul dam holds back one of the largest reservoirs in Central Asia.
Counted from the Naryn's source, the Syr Darya is over 3,000 km long.
The town of Naryn lies at about 2,000 m above sea level.

q.q: Which river does the Naryn help to form?

Q2216.t: An icefield's river winding north through boreal forest
Q2216.s: The Athabasca begins as meltwater from the Columbia Icefield and ends some 1,200 km later in a vast delta on Lake Athabasca. In between, as here, it winds north through an endless boreal forest of spruce, poplar and muskeg. Downstream of Fort McMurray, open-pit oil sands mines spread across the forest along its banks, plainly visible from the air.
Q2216.w: A wide brown river snaking through dark boreal forest dotted with bogs and small lakes.
f: The Athabasca Glacier, where the river begins, is one of the most visited glaciers in North America.
The Peace–Athabasca Delta at its mouth is one of the largest freshwater deltas in the world.
Its name comes from a Cree word describing reeds or grasses growing here and there.

q.q: Where does the Athabasca River begin?

Q1256528.s: In Burkina Faso it is called the Mouhoun. The river rises near Bobo-Dioulasso, runs north-east for a long way, then turns sharply and heads south, as it does here, through wooded savanna and farm plots. Later its dark-green band marks borders with Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana before it ends in Lake Volta, one of the world's largest reservoirs by area.
Q1256528.w: A dark ribbon of gallery forest winding south through dry, patchy savanna and small fields.
f: The Black Volta meets the White Volta in Lake Volta, in Ghana.
Lake Volta, which it feeds, covers about 8,500 km².
The river is about 1,350 km long.

q.q: What is the Black Volta called in Burkina Faso?

Q1644776.t: Where the Xingu begins, between forest and soy
Q1644776.s: The Culuene is the main headstream of the Xingu, flowing north across the Mato Grosso plateau. Here a dark ribbon of forest follows it through a landscape largely turned into vast soy and cattle farms. Downstream it enters the Xingu Indigenous Park, where the forest suddenly becomes unbroken, a boundary so sharp it shows up from space.
Q1644776.w: A dark, forest-lined river winding north across a checkerboard of enormous pale fields; further north, solid green forest.
f: The Xingu Indigenous Park, created in 1961, was the first large indigenous territory recognised in Brazil.
Peoples of the upper Xingu hold the Kuarup, a great ceremony honouring the dead.
With the Ronuro and other rivers, the Culuene forms the Xingu.

q.q: Which great river does the Culuene help to form?

Q191314.t: The 'Ganges of the South', held back in a wide lake
Q191314.s: Indians call it Dakshina Ganga, the Ganges of the South, and it is India's second-longest river after the Ganges itself. Here in Telangana the Sriram Sagar dam holds it in a wide, branching lake among dry, rocky plains. From its source near Nashik, only about 80 km from the Arabian Sea, it crosses the whole peninsula to the Bay of Bengal.
Q191314.w: A broad, branching reservoir with ragged fingers in flat, dry country, the river continuing east as a pale sandy ribbon.
f: The Godavari runs about 1,465 km, ending in a wide delta on the Bay of Bengal.
The Pushkaram bathing festival is held on the Godavari once every 12 years.
Sriram Sagar was built mainly to irrigate the dry plains of northern Telangana.

q.q: What is the Godavari's popular nickname?

Q124653.t: A steppe river on its way to Siberia's old capital
Q124653.s: Birch groves scattered like islands, round lakes by the hundred and ploughed steppe: the Tobol winds through this West Siberian plain in tight loops. It rises in Kazakhstan and runs about 1,600 km north to join the Irtysh at Tobolsk, the town named after it. Tobolsk was once the capital of all Siberia.
Q124653.w: A tightly looping river across flat steppe dotted with birch copses and countless round lakes.
f: Tobolsk, at its mouth, has the only stone kremlin in Siberia.
Dmitri Mendeleev, creator of the periodic table, was born in Tobolsk in 1834.
Its tributary the Tura carried Yermak's Cossacks deep into Siberia in the 1580s.

q.q: Which famous scientist was born in Tobolsk?

Q8197.t: One river, two names, three countries
Q8197.s: In Belarus and Russia it is the Western Dvina; in Latvia, the Daugava. Here it curves through Polotsk, one of the oldest towns of the Eastern Slavs, first mentioned in the chronicles in 862. From here it winds on through lake-studded forest and farmland to the Gulf of Riga, about 1,000 km from its source.
Q8197.w: A winding river through forest and farmland, a town spread across both banks and many small lakes scattered around.
f: Its source lies in the Valdai Hills, close to the sources of the Volga and the Dnieper.
In Latvia three hydropower dams turn the river into a chain of reservoirs.
Riga grew up near its mouth and became a major Hanseatic port.

q.q: What is the Daugava called in Belarus and Russia?

Q200174.t: Where an Amazon source bursts out of the Andes
Q200174.s: For hundreds of kilometres the Marañón runs north through one of the deepest canyons in the Andes; here it swings east and cuts its way out of the mountains through narrow gorges called pongos. Beyond them lies the endless green of the Amazon lowlands. Downstream it meets the Ucayali, and from that confluence on the river is called the Amazon.
Q200174.w: A brown river forcing its way through forested ridges in narrow gaps, then spreading into flat, endless rainforest to the east.
f: For centuries the Marañón was regarded as the main source of the Amazon.
In places its canyon in northern Peru is deeper than the Grand Canyon.
The Marañón is about 1,700 km long.

q.q: Which river does the Marañón meet to form the Amazon?

Q269710.t: A gold-rush river cut deep into the plateau
Q269710.s: The Fraser here runs in a deep trench carved into the forested Interior Plateau, with the Quesnel River joining it at the town of Quesnel. In the 1860s this was the gateway to the Cariboo gold fields, and thousands of miners came up the valley. At about 1,375 km, the Fraser is the longest river in British Columbia.
Q269710.w: A brown river in a deep, steep-sided trench across a forested plateau patched with clearings, a town at a river junction.
f: Simon Fraser followed the river to the sea in 1808, and it bears his name.
In good years millions of salmon swim up the Fraser to spawn.
Downstream it squeezes through Hell's Gate, a gorge only about 35 m wide.

q.q: Which fish runs up the Fraser in millions to spawn?

Q82207.t: A river born near one of the coldest villages on Earth
Q82207.s: The Indigirka starts its journey near Oymyakon, where winter temperatures have dropped close to −70 °C. It then cuts north through bare, rocky ranges, braiding into gravel channels, before spreading out across lake-strewn lowlands to the East Siberian Sea. For about eight months a year it lies frozen, a white line through the mountains.
Q82207.w: A pale, braided river among bare grey-brown mountains, patched with snow for much of the year.
f: Russkoye Ustye, in its delta, was settled by Russians in the 17th century, who kept their old speech and songs.
The Indigirka is about 1,700 km long.
It usually freezes in October and stays frozen until late May or June.

q.q: Which famously cold village lies on the Indigirka's upper course?

Q65383.t: The tributary longer than the river it joins
Q65383.s: Sandbanks glowing pale against dark taiga, oxbow lakes and long meanders: the Vychegda crosses the Komi Republic like this for hundreds of kilometres. Near Syktyvkar, the capital of Komi, it takes in the Sysola. At about 1,130 km it is longer than the Northern Dvina itself, which it joins at Kotlas.
Q65383.w: A wide meandering river with bright sandbanks and silver oxbow lakes in dark taiga, a city to the south-east.
f: Syktyvkar means 'town on the Sysola' in the Komi language.
In the 14th century Stephen of Perm preached along the Vychegda and created an alphabet for the Komi language.
The Vychegda is the largest tributary of the Northern Dvina.

q.q: Which river does the Vychegda join at Kotlas?

ne-rv-1159113559.t: The reddish river where Patagonia begins
ne-rv-1159113559.s: Colorado means 'reddish', for the silt that tints its water. The river rises in the Andes and runs south-east for roughly 1,000 km to the Atlantic, and by long tradition it marks the northern edge of Patagonia. Here it crosses dry, gravelly steppe in a thin green line, also serving as a border between Argentine provinces.
ne-rv-1159113559.w: A thin river with a narrow green fringe winding south-east across bare, pale-brown gravel plains.
f: It is formed by the Grande and the Barrancas rivers, which meet in the Andean foothills.
The river separates Mendoza from Neuquén, then La Pampa from Río Negro.
The Casa de Piedra dam downstream holds a large reservoir in the dry plains.

q.q: Which region traditionally begins south of the Río Colorado?

Q8542.t: A mountain river with two countries on its banks
Q8542.s: Deep in a gorge between huge bare mountains, the Panj runs grey-green and fast, with villages and orchards clinging to fans of gravel on both banks. On one side lies Tajikistan, on the other Afghanistan; the river is the border for hundreds of kilometres. Downstream it meets the Vakhsh, and together they become the Amu Darya.
Q8542.w: A thin river at the bottom of a deep gorge between massive bare ranges, small green patches of villages on both sides.
f: Its headwaters include the Pamir River, which flows out of Lake Zorkul.
In 1838 the British explorer John Wood reached Lake Zorkul and hailed it as the source of the Oxus.
Panj is the Persian word for 'five'.

q.q: The Panj and which other river form the Amu Darya?

Q49544.t: A clear, rocky river in a land of forest and cattle
Q49544.s: Unlike the muddy Amazon, the Xingu runs clear and dark green over rocks and rapids, spattered with forested islands. Around São Félix do Xingu, cattle pasture has cut into the forest in huge pale blocks, while the Kayapó indigenous lands nearby remain solid green. The river flows north for well over 1,500 km before merging into the Amazon.
Q49544.w: A wide, dark river full of rocky islands and rapids, pale blocks of pasture on one side and unbroken forest on the other.
f: Its rapids are home to fish found nowhere else, such as the black-and-white zebra pleco.
Near its mouth the river widens into a lake-like channel several kilometres across.
Its headwaters lie in the Xingu Indigenous Park, far to the south in Mato Grosso.

q.q: Which striped fish lives only in the rapids of the Xingu?

Q8493.t: A braided desert river that once filled the Aral Sea
Q8493.s: Two deserts face each other across the Amu Darya: the Karakum on one side, the Kyzylkum on the other. Between them the river spreads into a wide brown bed of shifting channels and sandbars, edged by a thin green strip of fields. Its water once filled the Aral Sea, but so much is now taken for irrigation that it rarely reaches the old shore.
Q8493.w: A wide, braided brown river with sandbars and a thin green strip of fields, pale desert on both sides.
f: The Karakum Canal carries its water westward across the desert for more than 1,000 km.
Counted from its Pamir sources, the Amu Darya is about 2,500 km long.
Khiva and the other oasis towns of Khorezm grew up on its lower course.

q.q: Which desert faces the Kyzylkum across the Amu Darya?

Q752674.t: A blue river of rapids in the southern Amazon
Q752674.s: The Tapajós is a clear-water river: in the dry season it runs blue-green over rocks and rapids, striking against the dense forest. Downstream it widens into a huge, lake-like channel with white sand beaches before meeting the muddy Amazon at Santarém, where the two waters flow side by side. It is formed by the Juruena and the Teles Pires.
Q752674.w: A dark blue-green river with rocky rapids and islands, winding north through dense forest cut by a few clearings and roads.
f: In 1928 Henry Ford founded Fordlândia on its banks to grow rubber for his cars.
Alter do Chão, near its mouth, is famous for white river beaches and is often called the Amazon's Caribbean.
Near Santarém the Tapajós is more than 10 km wide in places.

q.q: Which industrialist built a rubber town on the Tapajós?

Q204040.t: An Alpine river that ends in 'Europe's Amazon'
Q204040.s: The Mur starts high in the Austrian Alps and flows through Graz, but here on the Pannonian plain it has turned wild: a winding, willow-lined river with gravel bars and backwaters, marking borders as it goes. Soon it meets the Drava, and its floodplains form part of a vast protected wetland along the Mura, Drava and Danube.
Q204040.w: A winding river lined with dark floodplain forest and backwaters, crossing flat farmland patterned in long narrow strips.
f: In 2021 UNESCO named the Mura–Drava–Danube area the world's first five-country biosphere reserve.
The Mur flows through Graz, Austria's second-largest city.
Along its lower course it forms parts of the borders of Austria, Slovenia, Croatia and Hungary.

q.q: Which Austrian city does the Mur flow through?

Q979518.s: A milky-brown river swings in wide loops through the forests and plantations of Central Kalimantan. For people here the Barito has long been the main road, carrying boats, logs and coal barges down to the coast. At its mouth stands Banjarmasin, a city of canals whose floating markets trade from boats at dawn.
Q979518.w: A wide brown river looping through dark green forest and paler plantation blocks, with small towns on the bends.
f: The Barito is about 900 km long, one of the longest rivers of Borneo.
Banjarmasin is nicknamed the 'city of a thousand rivers' for its many canals.
Proboscis monkeys live in the mangroves and riverside forests of its lower course.

q.q: Which city stands at the mouth of the Barito?

Q135477.t: The river that keeps Lake Chad alive
Q135477.s: Most of the water that reaches Lake Chad comes down this river. The Chari rises in the Central African Republic and flows north-west for about 1,400 km, meandering through wide grassy floodplains that turn to marsh in the rainy season. At N'Djamena it meets the Logone, and together they run on to the lake.
Q135477.w: A broad, winding river with a wide, pale floodplain of grass and marsh, crossing flat savanna dotted with trees.
f: The Chari supplies about 90% of the water that flows into Lake Chad.
Lake Chad has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s, which makes this inflow all the more vital.
N'Djamena, the capital of Chad, stands at the meeting of the Chari and the Logone.

q.q: Which lake does the Chari feed?

Q131210.t: A river that twists through its canyon like a ribbon
Q131210.s: Few rivers loop as extravagantly as the Dniester here: it coils through a deep canyon cut into the Podolian plateau, bend after bend, between wooded slopes and pale rocky cliffs. Part of the canyon is now flooded behind a dam, forming a long, sinuous reservoir. The river runs about 1,350 km from the Carpathians to the Black Sea.
Q131210.w: A winding, snake-like river and reservoir in a deep wooded canyon, carved into a flat plateau of fields.
f: The Dniester rises in the Carpathians, not far from the Polish border.
Khotyn Fortress, on a bluff above the river upstream, dates back to the Middle Ages.
It ends in the Dniester Estuary, a wide lagoon behind a sandbar on the Black Sea.

q.q: In which mountains does the Dniester rise?

Q60067.t: Alaska's winter highway of river ice
Q60067.s: In summer the Kuskokwim is a wide, silty river looping through spruce forest and tundra; in winter it freezes so hard that people drive trucks and snowmobiles along it between villages. About 1,100 km long and without a single dam, it is the longest free-flowing river entirely within the United States. Its lower course crosses a flat delta freckled with lakes.
Q60067.w: A wide grey-brown river looping through dark spruce and tundra, with oxbow lakes and gravel bars along its banks.
f: The Kuskokwim 300 sled dog race starts and ends at Bethel, on its lower course.
Its lower basin is part of the Yukon–Kuskokwim Delta, one of the largest river deltas in the world.
Salmon from the Kuskokwim have fed Yup'ik villages along its banks for thousands of years.

q.q: Which town on the Kuskokwim hosts a famous sled dog race?

Q393769.t: A glacial river of grey silt below the Alaska Range
Q393769.s: Milky grey with glacial silt, the Tanana spreads into a maze of braided channels across a wide gravel floodplain, with the snowy wall of the Alaska Range to the south. Near Big Delta the Trans-Alaska Pipeline crosses it on its own suspension bridge. The river flows about 940 km north-west to the Yukon, passing close to Fairbanks.
Q393769.w: A wide, grey braided river on a broad gravel floodplain, snowy peaks of the Alaska Range rising to the south.
f: Since 1917 people in Nenana have bet on the exact minute the Tanana's ice breaks up in spring.
The Alaska Highway ends at Delta Junction, just south of the river.
Its grey colour comes from rock flour ground up by glaciers in the Alaska Range.

q.q: What do people bet on each spring at Nenana on the Tanana?
q.a: When the river ice breaks up

Q284603.t: The river that named a caribou herd
Q284603.s: Old Crow, the only community in Yukon without a road, stands on a bend of the Porcupine well north of the Arctic Circle. Around it the Old Crow Flats spread out as a vast sheet of lakes and ponds, glittering in summer. The river flows west into Alaska and joins the Yukon at Fort Yukon, about 900 km from its source.
Q284603.w: A winding river through flat, lake-strewn tundra and thin spruce, with a small village on a river bend.
f: The Porcupine caribou herd, roughly 200,000 animals, is named after this river.
The Old Crow Flats hold thousands of lakes and ponds and are a protected wetland.
Old Crow is home to the Vuntut Gwitchin, whose name means 'people of the lakes'.

q.q: Which animal herd is named after the Porcupine River?

Q1546553.t: A river of endless oxbows in the Alaskan wilds
Q1546553.s: The Koyukuk is a lesson in how rivers wander: tight loops, cut-off oxbow lakes and crescent-shaped scars fill its broad, wooded valley. It rises in the Brooks Range north of the Arctic Circle and flows about 680 km south-west to the Yukon. Only a handful of small villages stand on its banks.
Q1546553.w: A heavily meandering river surrounded by countless oxbow lakes and crescent-shaped ponds in dark spruce forest.
f: Gold strikes around Wiseman and Coldfoot, on its upper course, drew miners around 1900.
The Nogahabara Dunes, a field of active sand dunes, lie within its wildlife refuge.
The Koyukuk joins the Yukon at the village that shares its name.

q.q: Which great river does the Koyukuk flow into?

ne-rv-1159114673.t: An Ethiopian highland river heading for Somalia
ne-rv-1159114673.s: Rain on the Bale Mountains, some of the highest land in Ethiopia, feeds the Genale. It drops south-east from the highlands into dry, bushy lowlands, where it winds in a green thread of riverside trees. At Dolo, close to where Ethiopia, Kenya and Somalia meet, it joins the Dawa, and together they become the Jubba.
ne-rv-1159114673.w: A thin green line of trees along a winding river, crossing dry, reddish bush country that falls away from the highlands.
f: The Bale Mountains at its source are home to the Ethiopian wolf, the world's rarest canid.
It is the main headstream of the Jubba, one of Somalia's two great rivers.
Its upper course is also known as the Ganale Doria.

q.q: The Genale and the Dawa join to form which river?

Q559283.t: A Karakoram river feeding a Silk Road oasis
Q559283.s: The Yarkand comes down from glaciers of the Karakoram, grey with silt, and fans out into a braided channel as it leaves the mountains for the Tarim Basin. Its water sustains one of the great oases on the southern edge of the Taklamakan: Yarkant, an old Silk Road town. Downstream it is the longest source of the Tarim River.
Q559283.w: A grey, braided river fanning out from bare mountains onto a desert plain, with a big green oasis of fields beside it.
f: The Yarkand is about 1,100 km long.
Yarkant was for centuries a caravan town on the southern Silk Road, between Kashgar and Khotan.
Its headwaters lie among Karakoram glaciers above 5,000 m.

q.q: Which river does the Yarkand help to form?

Q1241991.t: A fur-trade river crossing the great northern bogs
Q1241991.s: Near here the Albany leaves the rocky Canadian Shield for the Hudson Bay Lowlands, one of the largest wetlands on Earth, where bogs and fens form stripes and teardrop shapes. The river runs about 980 km from Lake St. Joseph to James Bay. At its mouth, Fort Albany was one of the Hudson's Bay Company's earliest trading posts.
Q1241991.w: A broad brown river winding east through dark spruce and vast bogs patterned with stripes and pools.
f: The Hudson's Bay Company set up its post at the mouth of the Albany in the 1670s.
Since 1943 the Ogoki Diversion has sent part of its upper water south into the Great Lakes.
At about 980 km, the Albany is one of the longest rivers in Ontario.

q.q: Where does the Albany River end?

Q81555.t: A lonely northern river of the lost town Mangazeya
Q81555.s: Pale bogs, thousands of small lakes and thin larch forest stretch to the horizon as the Taz meanders north across the West Siberian Plain. About 1,400 km long, it ends in the Taz Estuary, a long arm of the Gulf of Ob. In the 17th century the fur-trading town of Mangazeya thrived on its lower course, then was abandoned.
Q81555.w: A winding river through flat, pale bog and larch woodland spattered with countless small lakes.
f: Mangazeya, founded around 1601, was nicknamed 'gold-boiling' for the wealth of its fur trade.
The Selkup people have fished and herded reindeer along the Taz for centuries.
The river stays frozen for more than half the year.

q.q: Which 17th-century fur town stood on the Taz?

Q1063190.t: A green river of old trading towns in western Hunan
Q1063190.s: The Yuan winds north-east through the forested hills of western Hunan, past terraced fields and old river towns. Hongjiang, on its bank here, grew rich for centuries shipping timber, tung oil and salt by boat. After more than 1,000 km, the river empties into Dongting Lake, one of China's great freshwater lakes.
Q1063190.w: A winding green river between wooded ridges and terraced fields, with small towns clustered on its bends.
f: Taoyuan county on the lower Yuan claims to be the setting of Tao Yuanming's tale 'Peach Blossom Spring'.
In Guizhou, where it rises, the river is called the Qingshui.
The Yuan is about 1,030 km long.

q.q: Which lake does the Yuan River flow into?

Q1068297.t: Atlanta's river, stretched into long lakes
Q1068297.s: A long reservoir with dozens of branching fingers spreads through the Georgia woods here: West Point Lake, one of several on the Chattahoochee. The river rises in the Blue Ridge Mountains, supplies most of metro Atlanta's water, and then forms the border between Georgia and Alabama. Far to the south it joins the Flint to become the Apalachicola.
Q1068297.w: A long, many-fingered reservoir along a river in rolling forest and farmland on the Georgia–Alabama border.
f: Lake Lanier, upstream, provides most of the drinking water for metro Atlanta.
The river runs about 690 km, from the Blue Ridge to Lake Seminole.
A national recreation area protects a green strip of the river inside metro Atlanta.

q.q: Which river does the Chattahoochee join to form the Apalachicola?

Q558643.t: A slow, looping river through the Black Belt
Q558643.s: The Alabama River takes its time, looping in wide, lazy meanders through the Black Belt, a crescent of dark, fertile soil that once grew much of the South's cotton. It forms near Montgomery where the Coosa and the Tallapoosa meet, and joins the Tombigbee north of Mobile. In 1965 civil rights marchers set out from Selma across the Edmund Pettus Bridge over this river.
Q558643.w: A brown river swinging in wide loops through a patchwork of dark fields, pine plantations and a long, narrow reservoir.
f: The Black Belt region takes its name from its dark, rich soil.
With the Tombigbee it forms the Mobile River, which drains into Mobile Bay.
The river is about 500 km long.

q.q: Which two rivers meet to form the Alabama?
x: The Tombigbee and the Black Warrior

Q602.t: A strong river in a corridor of vineyards
Q602.s: South of Lyon the Rhône runs straight and strong through a narrow corridor, with vineyards on its steep slopes and a road, a railway and a motorway squeezed along its banks. This is the heart of the northern Côtes du Rhône: Côte-Rôtie and Condrieu lie just upstream. From its Swiss glacier, the river runs about 810 km to its delta in the Camargue.
Q602.w: A wide river running north–south in a narrow valley, lined by canals, roads and railways, with steep hillsides on its west bank.
f: The Rhône starts at the Rhône Glacier in the Swiss Alps and passes through Lake Geneva.
It carries more water to the sea than any other French river.
The cold mistral wind funnels down this valley towards the Mediterranean.

q.q: Which lake does the Rhône flow through before entering France?

Q171675.t: The longest of the five rivers of Punjab
Q171675.s: Punjab means 'five waters', and the Sutlej is the longest of the five. It rises in Tibet near the sacred lakes below Mount Kailash, cuts straight through the Himalaya in deep gorges, and then crosses the flat plains of Punjab. Here its wide, sandy bed often carries only a narrow stream, as much of its water is taken for irrigation upstream.
Q171675.w: A wide, pale sandy riverbed with a thin braided stream, across a flat green grid of irrigated fields.
f: The Sutlej is about 1,450 km long.
It is one of the few rivers that cut right across the main Himalayan range.
Joined by the Chenab, it becomes the Panjnad, which flows into the Indus.

q.q: What does the name Punjab mean?

Q798339.t: A wild tundra river racing to the Arctic Ocean
Q798339.s: Almost 1,000 km of lakes, rapids and falls, and hardly a tree for most of the way: the Back River crosses the barren lands of Nunavut to the Arctic Ocean. It is named after George Back, a British naval officer who travelled down it in 1834. For most of the year it lies frozen under snow.
Q798339.w: A river threading a chain of irregular lakes and white rapids across bare, rolling tundra speckled with ponds.
f: It was once known as the Great Fish River.
It reaches the sea at Chantrey Inlet, on the Arctic coast.
Along its course the river drops through dozens of rapids.

q.q: What was the Back River once called?

Q2242.t: Rocky Mountain water on its way across the prairie
Q2242.s: The line on the map here traces the Bow River, the South Saskatchewan's main headstream, just downstream of Calgary. Born at Bow Lake in Banff National Park, it runs clear and green across rolling prairie, lined with cottonwoods. Further east it meets the Oldman to form the South Saskatchewan, which carries the water on across the dry plains.
Q2242.w: A green river winding south-east across prairie fields and round irrigation circles, with Calgary's sprawl just to the north-west.
f: Counting from the Bow's source, the South Saskatchewan system runs well over 1,000 km.
Lake Diefenbaker, a large reservoir on the South Saskatchewan, supplies water across much of southern Saskatchewan.
Below Calgary the Bow is famous among anglers for its trout.

q.q: Which two rivers meet to form the South Saskatchewan?
x: The Red Deer and the Bow

Q1259188.t: Burkina's Nakambé, pooled behind the Bagré dam
Q1259188.s: In Burkina Faso the White Volta is called the Nakambé. Here in the south of the country it is held back by the Bagré dam, spreading into a long, branching lake among dry savanna and small farms. Downstream it crosses into Ghana, flows through the northern plains not far from Tamale, and ends in the vast Lake Volta.
Q1259188.w: A long, branching reservoir in dry, tan savanna dotted with trees and small fields, fed from the north.
f: The Bagré dam supplies water for rice fields and hydropower in southern Burkina Faso.
The White Volta rises in northern Burkina Faso, towards the edge of the Sahel.
Its tributary the Red Volta joins it just across the border in Ghana.

q.q: What is the White Volta called in Burkina Faso?

Q875573.t: The river that gave the Han Chinese their name
Q875573.s: The name Han, borne by a dynasty and then by China's largest ethnic group, traces back to this river. Here on the Jianghan Plain it winds between dikes through a flat, watery land of rice fields, fish ponds and lakes. It joins the Yangtze at Wuhan, where the district of Hankou, 'Han mouth', stands at the confluence.
Q875573.w: A winding river between dikes across a flat plain of rice paddies, silver fish ponds and scattered lakes.
f: The Danjiangkou reservoir on its upper course sends water north towards Beijing along a canal over 1,000 km long.
About 1,500 km long, the Han is one of the Yangtze's largest tributaries.
Hankou, at its mouth, is one of the three towns that merged to form Wuhan.

q.q: At which city does the Han River meet the Yangtze?

Q271044.t: The 'great river' of India's rice bowl
Q271044.s: Mahanadi means 'great river' in Sanskrit. Here in Chhattisgarh its basin is a flat, green-and-gold plain of rice fields, crossed by wide, sandy riverbeds that fill only in the monsoon. Downstream in Odisha the river is held back by the Hirakud dam, then spreads into a broad delta on the Bay of Bengal.
Q271044.w: A wide, pale sandy riverbed with a thin stream, crossing a flat patchwork of rice fields and village ponds.
f: With its dikes, the Hirakud dam stretches for about 25 km, one of the longest dams in the world.
Chhattisgarh is often called the rice bowl of central India.
The Mahanadi is roughly 850 km long.

q.q: What does the name Mahanadi mean?

Q1535828.t: A West African river named by Portuguese sailors
Q1535828.s: Portuguese navigators named its mouth after Saint Andrew, and the name stuck to the whole river. The Sassandra runs south for about 650 km from the Guinean highlands, through savanna and then rainforest, to the Gulf of Guinea. Here it winds through mixed forest and farmland, some 200 km before the Buyo dam holds it back in a large lake.
Q1535828.w: A winding brown river through a mosaic of forest patches, plantations and fields, heading south towards a large reservoir.
f: Taï National Park, one of West Africa's last large rainforests, lies west of its lower course.
The Buyo reservoir on the Sassandra is one of the largest lakes in Côte d'Ivoire.
The river reaches the sea at the small port town of Sassandra.

q.q: Which saint is the name Sassandra thought to come from?

Q3292.t: Lake Winnipeg's outlet, harnessed on its way to the Bay
Q3292.s: Everything that drains into Lake Winnipeg, from the Rockies to the edge of Ontario, leaves through the Nelson. The river runs about 640 km north-east across the Canadian Shield to Hudson Bay, and on its lower course a chain of big dams turns its power into electricity for Manitoba. Around it lie endless spruce forest, bog and lakes.
Q3292.w: A wide river cutting north-east through dark spruce and pale bog, with dams and long reservoirs along its lower course.
f: Thomas Button named it in 1612 after Robert Nelson, his ship's master, who died there.
York Factory, near its mouth, was long the Hudson's Bay Company's main depot on the Bay.
Its basin covers about a million km² in Canada and the United States.

q.q: Which lake does the Nelson River drain?

Q1229.t: A quiet steppe river under white chalk cliffs
Q1229.s: White chalk cliffs rise on the Don's right bank, bright against green woods and yellow fields, while the left bank spreads into a low floodplain of meadows, oxbows and sandbars. The Don runs about 1,870 km from near Tula to the Sea of Azov. The ancient Greeks knew it as the Tanais and saw it as the boundary between Europe and Asia.
Q1229.w: A winding river with pale chalk cliffs on one side and a wide green floodplain with oxbow lakes on the other.
f: Mikhail Sholokhov's novel And Quiet Flows the Don is set among the Cossacks of its middle course.
The Volga–Don Canal, opened in 1952, links it with the Volga near Volgograd.
The Don ends in the Sea of Azov, often called the shallowest sea in the world.

q.q: Which sea does the Don flow into?

Q1046685.t: The river that gave Jiangxi its short name
Q1046685.s: Jiangxi province's one-character name, Gan, comes from this river, which runs the length of the province from south to north. Here it winds through red hills and bright green rice paddies near Taihe. After about 750 km it spreads into Poyang Lake, China's largest freshwater lake, which drains into the Yangtze.
Q1046685.w: A wide, winding river through a patchwork of red-earth hills and green rice paddies, with sandbars on the bends.
f: Nanchang, Jiangxi's capital, stands on the Gan; its Tengwang Pavilion is one of China's most famous towers.
The upper Gan was once feared for its 'eighteen rapids', now largely tamed by dams.
Poyang Lake, where it ends, swells hugely in the summer floods and shrinks in winter.

q.q: Which province's short name, Gan, comes from this river?

Q193499.t: A Deccan river of dams and legendary diamonds
Q193499.s: The Krishna crosses the dry Deccan plateau from west to east, and here it widens into the great Almatti reservoir, a sheet of water among brown fields. It rises in the Western Ghats near Mahabaleshwar and runs about 1,400 km to the Bay of Bengal. Some of history's most famous diamonds came from mines along its lower course.
Q193499.w: A broad, branching reservoir with jagged arms spreading over a flat, brown plateau of fields.
f: The Koh-i-Noor is thought to have come from the Kollur mine on the lower Krishna.
Nagarjuna Sagar dam, downstream, is one of the largest masonry dams in the world.
The Almatti dam stores water to irrigate the dry plains of northern Karnataka.

q.q: Which famous diamond is thought to come from a mine on the Krishna?

Q2249.t: The river where the Rocky Mountains end
Q2249.s: The Canadian Rockies run out at the Liard's valley, and here the river swings through their rugged northern tip in a canyon of rapids, with forested slopes and bare grey peaks around it. Its French name, from the fur traders, means 'cottonwood', after the poplars on its banks. It flows about 1,100 km to meet the Mackenzie at Fort Simpson.
Q2249.w: A green river winding through a deep forested valley between grey mountain ridges, with gravel bars on its bends.
f: Liard River Hot Springs, just upstream, is one of the largest natural hot springs in Canada.
Wood bison graze along the Alaska Highway near its valley.
Below Great Slave Lake, no river brings more water to the Mackenzie.

q.q: What does the fur traders' name Liard mean?

Q732790.t: A river of rapids between Angola and Congo
Q732790.s: The Kwango rises on the high plateaus of northern Angola and flows north for about 1,100 km through savanna and gallery forest, for a long stretch marking the border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Falls and rapids break its course. Downstream it joins the Kasai, and its water finally reaches the Congo River.
Q732790.w: A winding river with a dark ribbon of gallery forest across rolling, grassy plateau cut by small valleys.
f: The Kwango is the largest tributary of the Kasai.
Its valley in Angola is known for diamonds washed from the river gravels.
It meets the Kasai near the town of Bandundu.

q.q: Which river does the Kwango flow into?

Q846063.t: A river through Zambia's oldest national park
Q846063.s: The Kafue winds through one of Africa's great wildernesses: Kafue National Park, Zambia's oldest and largest, with wooded savanna, floodplains and grassy dambos stretching to the horizon. Upstream the river crosses the Copperbelt; downstream it spreads over the Kafue Flats, home to herds of lechwe antelope, before joining the Zambezi.
Q846063.w: A dark, winding river with pale floodplain grassland, through endless olive-green woodland dotted with shallow dambos.
f: Kafue National Park covers about 22,400 km², a little larger than Wales.
The Kafue lechwe, a water-loving antelope, lives only on the Kafue Flats.
At about 960 km, the Kafue is the longest river flowing entirely within Zambia.

q.q: Which antelope lives only on the Kafue Flats?

Q2742774.t: A river of gems and clay dolls in dry Minas Gerais
Q2742774.s: The Jequitinhonha rises near Diamantina, where diamonds were found in the 18th century, and flows north-east through dry hills of scrub and pasture to the Atlantic in Bahia. Its valley is famous across Brazil for folk art, especially painted clay dolls made by local women. Gemstones such as tourmaline and aquamarine are mined in its hills.
Q2742774.w: A winding, sandy river in a valley of rounded, dry hills, grey-green scrub and patches of pasture.
f: Diamantina, near its source, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
It runs about 1,100 km to the Atlantic at Belmonte, in Bahia.
The Irapé dam on its upper course is one of the tallest dams in Brazil.

q.q: What folk art is the Jequitinhonha valley famous for?

Q955354.t: A lonely river across Patagonia to Welsh villages
Q955354.s: For hundreds of kilometres the Chubut crosses almost empty Patagonian plateau, a thin green thread between ochre cliffs and grey-brown steppe. It rises in the Andes and runs about 800 km east to the Atlantic. In its lower valley Welsh settlers arrived in 1865, and towns like Gaiman still serve Welsh tea.
Q955354.w: A thin, winding green line across a vast brown plateau, with layered ochre cliffs along parts of the valley.
f: Some families in the Chubut valley still speak Welsh.
Fossils of Patagotitan, one of the largest known dinosaurs, were found in Chubut province.
The Florentino Ameghino dam holds a reservoir in a canyon on its lower course.

q.q: Settlers from which country arrived in the lower Chubut valley in 1865?

Q1162365.t: A salty river winding across the hot Chaco plain
Q1162365.s: Salado simply means 'salty', and the river earns the name: its water picks up salt from the dry soils it crosses. Rising in the Andes of Salta, where it is called the Juramento, it winds south-east for more than 1,000 km across the flat, scrubby plains of Santiago del Estero. It ends in the Paraná near Santa Fe.
Q1162365.w: A thin meandering river with pale banks, winding across flat olive-green scrub and large cleared fields.
f: Its upper course in Salta is known as the Pasaje or Juramento.
Summer temperatures on the plains it crosses can climb above 45 °C.
Other Argentine rivers share its name, so it is often called the Salado del Norte.

q.q: What does the river's name, Salado, mean?

Q1165761.t: The 'white river' of Brazil's far north
Q1165761.s: Branco means 'white', for its pale, silty water, which stands out among the dark rivers of the Amazon. Here it curves past Boa Vista, the only Brazilian state capital lying wholly north of the equator, across the open savannas of Roraima known as the lavrado. Downstream it enters the rainforest and flows into the Rio Negro.
Q1165761.w: A broad, pale river curving past a fan-shaped city, with open grassy savanna and scattered lakes around it.
f: Boa Vista's streets fan out from the riverbank in a radial plan that is easy to see from the air.
The Branco is formed by the Uraricoera and the Tacutu, which meet north of Boa Vista.
It is the largest river of the state of Roraima.

q.q: Which river does the Branco flow into?

Q655251.t: A great river of the Colombian llanos
Q655251.s: The llanos stretch flat to every horizon, green grassland striped with dark gallery forest, and through them the Meta loops east towards the Orinoco. In the rainy season much of this plain floods into a shimmering sheet of water; in the dry season it turns gold. Along its last stretch the river forms the border between Colombia and Venezuela.
Q655251.w: A broad, looping brown river with sandbars, crossing flat green grassland striped by dark lines of gallery forest.
f: The Meta is about 1,000 km long and one of the Orinoco's main tributaries.
It joins the Orinoco at Puerto Carreño.
Llaneros, the cowboys of the plains, have herded cattle along its banks for centuries.

q.q: Which river does the Meta flow into?

Q849693.t: A rainforest river rich in oxbow lakes
Q849693.s: The Madre de Dios is a textbook rainforest river: a broad brown ribbon swinging in huge loops, leaving oxbow lakes that glint like horseshoes in the green. It rises in the Andes near Manu National Park in Peru and flows east into Bolivia, where it joins the Beni. Giant otters and caimans live in its quiet lakes.
Q849693.w: A wide brown river looping through unbroken forest, with shining horseshoe-shaped lakes along its course.
f: Manu National Park, near its source, is one of the most biodiverse places on Earth.
Macaws gather in their hundreds at clay licks on its riverbanks.
Its name means 'Mother of God' in Spanish.

q.q: Which river does the Madre de Dios join in Bolivia?

ne-rv-1159116437.t: The river where Brazil's patron saint was found
ne-rv-1159116437.s: In 1717 three fishermen on the Paraíba do Sul pulled a small clay statue of the Virgin from the water near today's Aparecida; it became Our Lady Aparecida, patron saint of Brazil. The river runs along a long valley between the Serra do Mar and the Serra da Mantiqueira, linking the states of São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, and reaches the Atlantic after about 1,100 km.
ne-rv-1159116437.w: A winding river in a wide valley between two mountain ranges, lined with towns, a highway and farmland.
f: The basilica at Aparecida is one of the largest Catholic churches in the world.
Much of Rio de Janeiro's water supply is pumped from the Paraíba do Sul.
In the 19th century its valley was Brazil's great coffee-growing region.

q.q: What did fishermen pull from the Paraíba do Sul in 1717?
q.a: A statue of the Virgin Mary

Q18278.t: The river that gave a country its name
Q18278.s: A whole country took its name from this river: Uruguay lies on its eastern bank. Here, far upstream, the Uruguay is a green-brown river winding through rolling hills of forest and farmland, with Brazil on one bank and Argentina on the other. A little upstream it tumbles over the Moconá Falls, which run lengthwise along the river rather than across it.
Q18278.w: A winding river in a deep green valley between rolling hills, forest and patchwork farmland on its banks.
f: Uruguay's official name means 'Eastern Republic of the Uruguay' – the land east of this river.
It runs about 1,800 km and, with the Paraná, forms the Río de la Plata.
Its name is often translated from Guaraní as 'river of the painted birds'.

q.q: Which river joins the Uruguay to form the Río de la Plata?

Q21806688.t: A muddy river that loses itself in the Chaco
Q21806688.s: The Pilcomayo carries so much silt down from the Bolivian Andes that it keeps choking its own bed. Here it leaves the foothills and enters the flat Gran Chaco, where three countries meet on its banks. Further on, much of its water spills into shifting marshes, and its channel moves from year to year.
Q21806688.w: A pale, silty river with a wide sandy bed across flat, olive-green Chaco scrub, with dry channels branching off.
f: Its sediment load is among the highest of any river in the world.
It rises in the Andes of Bolivia, near Potosí.
For much of its course it forms the border between Argentina and Paraguay.

q.q: On which river do Argentina, Bolivia and Paraguay meet?

Q2635327.t: A dark rainforest river in bonobo country
Q2635327.s: Endless rainforest, broken only by the dark, twisting line of the Tshuapa: this is the heart of the Congo Basin. The river winds west for about 1,000 km, joining other streams to reach the Congo near Mbandaka, a city on the equator. Its basin lies south of the Congo River, the only region in the world where wild bonobos live.
Q2635327.w: A narrow, dark river twisting through unbroken, deep-green rainforest, its banks almost hidden by the canopy.
f: The province of Tshuapa, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, is named after the river.
Its water reaches the Congo by way of the Busira and the Ruki.
Salonga National Park, Africa's largest tropical rainforest reserve, lies to its south-west.

q.q: Which great ape lives wild only south of the Congo River?
